P1.evidence: Read back the setter: 'I know you spoke with Kim. He kind of gave me an overview, so I've got a head start on you.' Full four-part frame delivered: 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at ... really build out what it is that you want ... talk about what's held you back, and then if I feel like we can help you, we can talk about the coaching, and if not, that's fine as well.' Frame agreement was a thrown-away 'Alrighty?' answered with 'Yeah, sure' rather than a clean check. Open question verbatim: 'What were you hoping we could potentially help you with?'

P2.evidence: Only diet was actually asked — 'What's your diet like?' Age (35) came out incidentally when the prospect joked about getting older; height and weight were never established. Work was volunteered ('I'm working in films, so like in visual effects ... most of the time I'm sitting or standing in the standing desk') and the rep followed up on the business only as rapport. The prospect volunteered a lumbar protrusion, a knee problem and an operation the previous month and the rep asked no health or injury question at any point. Training week, results from current training, sleep and energy were never asked. Volunteered information the rep never asked for scores as a miss.

P3.evidence: Good six-month framing — 'if we were to fast forward six months, like what's the ultimate goal? Where do you want to be? Who is Carlo in six months?' — which surfaced fat loss, muscle and the pancake, but the aesthetics/function and 'something you can't do right now' prompts were never asked in their own right. The bridge to the real driver ran well: 'You said you want to take it more seriously now, I guess why? ... what shifted for you?' And the consequence-of-success question landed: 'What actually changes when you're at that point?' It then stopped at the individual — 'Who else does that impact?' was never asked, nothing was driven through to family or legacy, and there was no reflect-back. The prospect went to identity and business control himself and the rep followed him into business chat instead of deepening.

P4.evidence: Not run. The prospect handed the rep the phase unprompted — 'I tried like different methods, but I'm never really accountable, because I tried like things that are online, or like, or are not progressive' — and the entire response was 'Makes sense. Well, I'm sorry to hear you're not seeing the progress you want, man.' No 'what have you tried', no 'what happened with that', no 'why didn't it stick', no root-cause naming, and never 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?'

P5.evidence: Entirely absent. The two-year cost-of-inaction question was never asked, nor 'is that something you're willing to settle for', nor 'why not', nor the line in the sand. The prospect opened the door himself — 'I'm tired of repeating the same cycle over and over again' — and the rep moved toward price instead of amplifying it.

P6.evidence: The rep asked a weaker home-made variant — 'how committed would you say you are to actually taking it seriously and actually, like, really going for it and getting the structure in place' — and got a conditional answer: '100%, as long as the program is really serious and the price is something that I can handle.' He isolated the conditionality cleanly — 'Money aside and program aside ... how committed are you to yourself to make a change' — and got '100%'. Neither scripted question was asked: no 'do you believe you can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in your corner', no 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in'. He did wait for a clear yes before moving on.

P11.evidence: The call never reached a close attempt. The rep quoted 5,100 EUR for six months and tested affordability — 'is that something that's achievable for you if it is the right thing' — the prospect said no, and the rep closed the conversation out. No ask for the sale, no payment, no onboarding call, no agreement, no welcome email.

objection_plays.detail: The money objection was explicit — 'it's a big investment at the moment', 'too much at the moment' — and the rep ran one move then abandoned the play. He offered a value reframe ('I would say it depends, right? It depends on how important it is') and within two turns agreed with the prospect's own reasoning and ended it: 'since you're starting a business ... if that's the case I don't want to waste more of your time.' Nothing else from OC was attempted: no isolation ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%'), no 'you're not in a should-I place, you're in a how place', no offer to break the payment up, no request for an honest financial conversation, and none of the financial picture questions. The rep also supplied the prospect's excuse for him, which reinforced the objection rather than isolating it.

The prospect framed it as timing as much as money — 'too much at the moment', 'maybe we can speak later in another moment when it's time' — and no part of OD was run. No 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up'. The rep validated the deferral and offered to stay in touch.

Script gap. The prospect asked a direct programme-fit question in his opening answer — 'I want to know if I can integrate your program with what I'm really doing ... I would like to see if I can squeeze like three session training with you, and like two at the gym, or maybe it's too much' — and it was never answered at any point. There is no scripted move for a prospect who wants to keep an existing training modality alongside the programme.

Second script gap, and the more serious one. The prospect disclosed a lumbar vertebral protrusion, a knee problem and an operation one month earlier that had stopped him training, with a return date of 'the 6th'. The playbook has no clinical screening or medical-clearance step anywhere in P1-P6, so nothing prompted the rep to ask what the operation was or whether a clinician had cleared him for loaded kettlebell work. He asked nothing and moved to price.

notes: Frames and opens well and asks a genuinely good 'what shifted for you' bridge, then skips the entire middle of the process — no baseline, no root cause, no consequence frame — and goes from a soft commitment check straight to a number, with none of the three pillars presented. Because no pain was built and no cost of inaction established, the price landed on nothing and the deal died in about ninety seconds. Coaching priority: run P4 and P5 before quoting, and when a prospect volunteers recent surgery and a spinal issue, stop and screen it rather than moving to price.
